name: Jeiel
overview: Jeiel was a male member of the tribe of Reuben, identified specifically as a Reubenite in 1 Chronicles 5:7. His mention in Scripture is brief, and no additional personal details or notes are provided beyond his tribal affiliation and gender.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeiel means 'G-d has preserved,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of God's preservation. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 5:7 and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Jeiel was the son of Zechariah, as inferred from 1 Chronicles 5:7. Beyond this father-son relationship, no further family connections are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jeiel's significance lies primarily in his identification as a Reubenite, linking him to the tribe descended from Reuben, Jacob's firstborn son. His mention in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles situates him within the broader context of Israel's tribal history, underscoring the preservation of the Reubenite lineage. Although no specific deeds or roles are attributed to him, his inclusion reflects the biblical emphasis on genealogical continuity and God's faithfulness to His people.
